title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 8 (Acceptance by performing conditions, or receiving consideration)

content.overview: Section 8 provides that performance of the conditions of a proposal, or the acceptance of any consideration for a reciprocal promise which may be offered with a proposal, is an acceptance of the proposal.
content.glance: Performing the conditions of a proposal, or accepting consideration for a reciprocal promise offered with it, is acceptance.
content.study: Performance of the conditions of a proposal, or acceptance of any consideration for a reciprocal promise offered with a proposal, constitutes acceptance of the proposal. This covers acceptance by conduct without a formal communication of assent. Current-law framing: identify the conditions of the proposal or the offered consideration; test performance or acceptance of consideration; conclude that acceptance has occurred under s. 8.

sections.heading: Performance of conditions
sections.body: Performance of the conditions of a proposal is an acceptance of the proposal.

sections.heading: Acceptance of consideration
sections.body: Acceptance of any consideration for a reciprocal promise offered with a proposal is an acceptance of the proposal.

provisions.title: Acceptance by performing conditions, or receiving consideration

examples.title: Performance as acceptance
examples.body: A proposes that B do a specified act for a reward. B performs the act. That performance is acceptance under s. 8.

hypotheticals.question: Must acceptance always be communicated in words?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 8 treats performance of conditions or acceptance of consideration as acceptance.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-8
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Only a written or spoken assent can accept a proposal.
misconceptions.correction: Section 8 allows acceptance by performing the conditions of the proposal or by receiving consideration.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 8 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the conditions of the proposal or the offered consideration. II. Test performance or acceptance of consideration. III. Conclude acceptance under s. 8. IV. Link to s. 7 if absolute acceptance is in issue.

examTips: State both limbs: conditions and consideration.
Contrast with formal communication under ss. 3–4.
